task: E7 P1-9 full-printf RTC interval stability
evidence_scope: Historical WSL Ubuntu-22.04 logs; no simulator launched for this analysis.

stdout_requirements_observed: 11 full date/time printf lines for seconds 1 through 11
TIMER_CONFIG_OK with CPU frequency and Q16 coefficient

original_acceptance.mean: each run has 10 observed intervals and its mean is within 1s +/-5%

p1_three_run_status.reason: Only two matching full-printf runs exist in WSL evidence; no third matching Q16/image run was found, and this analysis did not launch a simulator.

causal_diagnosis.q16_calibration: In cache-phase, q16=8000 produced mean 0.866182s; the existing update rule round(8000 * 0.866182) yields q16=6929. The two q16=6929 runs then measured 0.967607s and 0.994096s. This supports the coefficient adjustment for that simulator image and host run context.
causal_diagnosis.host_vs_guest_clock: In the older same-image q16=8000 series, host means vary from 1.108064s to 2.749636s while all recorded guest max-lateness values are [767836]us. Host arrival intervals therefore include simulator/host throughput and scheduling effects that are not mirrored by the guest run-maximum lateness metric.
causal_diagnosis.per_interval_variation: The passing q16=6929 runs include individual intervals below 0.95s, but the specified acceptance is on the 10-interval mean and guest max lateness. Per-interval values are recorded descriptively; no new threshold was added.
causal_diagnosis.attribution_limit: RTC_DIAG reports one maximum over the whole guest run, without an interval index. It cannot identify which host interval contained the guest lateness. The observed host interval also combines printf, simulator output and host scheduling; per-tick guest lateness is not available in these logs.
